title: POST /game-api/s2s-api/v1.0/lobby/dedicatedServers/registerUnmanagedServer
$comment: Observed on 1.8.0.13, three runs (out/mitm-capture.jsonl, -A, -B): 200, 956-959 bytes, application/json, chunked with Expect: 100-continue. This is the call that registers a community dedicated server AND that returns ownerToken.bin - see docs/en/ArmaReforger_BackendAPI_EN.md section 3.3. Both shapes below are the captured ones; the request carries two fields server.json rejects (playerCountLimit, supportedGameClientTypes) because the server builds this body itself. One field appears only in a *re*-registration: accessToken, the ownerToken the profile already holds - and with it the backend answers with the same providerServerId, so the room survives a restart. That was established by running the server twice against one profile directory: the first registration carried no token and the second carried accessToken, with every other field identical except name, and both answers named the same providerServerId, while a third run with a fresh profile got a different one. A pinned dedicatedServerId in server.json is ignored: the answer's dedicatedServerId was different in both runs. See 'A room can be built, kept and used entirely over HTTP' in the backend document.

region.description: Empty in every captured request - the server did not set a region, and the answer echoes an empty region back.

name.description: The server's display name, game.name in server.json. The same value comes back inside dsConfig.game.name.

accessToken.description: **Present only in a re-registration**, and never in the first one: the ownerToken the profile already holds. Sending it makes the answer name the *same* providerServerId as before, which is what keeps a server's room - and its ban list - across restarts. A caller that holds a stored ownerToken can therefore rebuild the room itself, with no game server running.

playerCountLimit.description: game.maxPlayers. Rejected by the server.json schema and sent here anyway, because the server builds the body.

supportedGameClientTypes.description: The client platforms accepted. Also rejected by the server.json schema; the default is ["PLATFORM_PC"].

mods.description: The addon list, empty on a vanilla server. A configured mod is downloaded before this call, not after - see the Workshop schemas in this directory.

providerServerId.description: The server's identity as the backend sees it. It is the value the owner token carries as its serverId claim and the value rooms/register returns as roomId.

dedicatedServerId.description: The dedicated server's own id. Every later call sends it as dedicatedServerId (and as dedicatedHostId in rooms/register, and as id in the heartbeat).

region.description: Echoed from the request; empty in the captures.

tags.description: Empty in the captures; the field is not present in the request, so the backend adds it.

ownerToken.description: The server writes this string, unchanged, to $profile:ownerToken.bin and then sends it back as accessToken on every later call. Its payload carries iat, serverId, serverType and ownerType. See docs/en/ArmaReforger_Profile_EN.md section 3.
